clusters.title: Bot records wrong quantity or unit
clusters.plain_summary: The bot misinterprets the buyer's quantity or unit, leading to incorrect lead details. This hurts the lead because sellers get mismatched requirements, causing failed connections.

examples.trigger: buyer: Said the number five twice ("Panch Panch"). | bot: Recorded it as 55 Kg instead of 5 Kg.
buyer: Asked for 100 cartons at least. | bot: Read back 400 cartons and a pack size the buyer never gave, though 100 was recorded.
buyer: Never gave a quantity. | bot: Recorded a quantity anyway.
buyer: Never gave a unit. | bot: Recorded a unit anyway.

fix.change: When a buyer explicitly states a custom unit (e.g., 'pair' / पेयर), preserve it exactly as spoken instead of mapping it to the default system unit (e.g., 'piece' / पीस). If the buyer never states a unit, do not invent one; leave it blank and proceed to seller connection.
fix.where: After [para 55] Assemble before you respond and before [para 148] Product-context inference
fix.already_covered: [para 55] Assemble before you respond and [para 58] Advance and capture silently cover capturing partial info and not re-asking, but lack explicit rules to preserve custom units and avoid hallucinating missing quantities/units.
fix.risk: May cause the bot to retain non-standard units like 'pair' which might confuse downstream filtering if the system strictly expects standard metric/imperial units.
fix.test_buyer: Buyer: 'I need 10 pairs of these shoes.' Bot should record 10 pairs, not 10 pieces. Buyer: 'I need 5.' Bot should record 5 with no unit instead of defaulting to 5 Kg.

clusters.title: Bot misclassifies product or spec
clusters.plain_summary: The bot assigns the wrong product category or specification due to ASR errors or poor context. This hurts the lead because the wrong sellers are contacted.

examples.trigger: buyer: Named the brand "Dubai Kunafa". | bot: Recorded "Dubai Kona".
buyer: Said "hanji Sir ji" (yes, sir). | bot: Replied as if the buyer had said to wait; the vendor transcript read "hold on, hanji sir ji".
buyer: Wanted a soil dumping service. | bot: Put the lead under Tipper Trucks and recorded the answer as "10 wheeler".
buyer: Wanted a service with no matching product category. | bot: Mapped it to the nearest wrong category.

fix.change: After a language mismatch or mode switch, always resume the requirement collection flow by asking the first unanswered question from the current product's phase instead of staying stuck in language resolution.
fix.risk: This might cause the bot to prematurely skip collection if it misinterprets a brief language-related response as a refusal to provide specs, potentially reducing lead quality.
fix.test_buyer: Buyer says 'I need 540 kilos of sugar-free figs with no jaggery' and the bot switches to Hindi. After the language mismatch is resolved, the bot must immediately resume asking for missing quantity and color attributes instead of remaining in language resolution mode.

clusters.title: Bot misses buyer's specifications
clusters.plain_summary: The bot fails to capture details the buyer explicitly states, such as size, color, or custom specs. This hurts the lead because the lead is incomplete for the seller.

examples.trigger: buyer: Said the use is a pharmacy college. | bot: Recorded "hospital use", the nearest listed option.
buyer: Asked for a "chote dhakkan wali" (small-cap) one. | bot: Recorded "1/2 inch", which was not even in the option list.
buyer: Gave the quantity as 20 "peti" (cartons). | bot: Recorded the unit as "pack"; the auditor ruled peti is not a pack.
buyer: Said they want all grit sizes. | bot: Recorded a single size, 500.

fix.change: When the buyer gives multiple specs, context, or custom values in one breath, capture all of them immediately instead of picking only the nearest listed option. If the buyer provides a custom value that is unrelated or unclear, mark it as AMBIGUOUS and re-ask only that specific field; never overwrite a valid captured spec with an incorrect nearest option.
fix.where: para 149 (Context-aware extraction) and para 1068 (Capture future fields immediately)
fix.risk: The bot might capture more values than intended, potentially misattributing context to the wrong specification if surrounding context is ambiguous.
fix.test_buyer: A buyer says: 'I need a chote dhakkan wali, 20 peti, all grit sizes, G+1 building, 18 by 15 feet, for cylinder testing, six or twelve meter lifting height, and what are the brand options?'. The bot must capture all these specs and ask for the missing quantity, instead of recording only one size, one unit, or ignoring custom values.

clusters.title: Bot loops or repeats itself
clusters.plain_summary: The bot gets stuck in a loop or repeats the same sentence multiple times instead of moving the conversation forward. This hurts the lead because it frustrates the buyer and wastes time.

examples.trigger: buyer: Waited to be transferred. | bot: Said the call would be transferred, then restarted the whole call flow, five times.
buyer: Waited to be transferred. | bot: Said it would transfer but never did; the record says Transferred, which is wrong.
buyer: Was being transferred. | bot: Said the whole transfer sentence twice in one go.
buyer: Was waiting on the line. | bot: Said "good sellers are available on the line" twice.
examples.quote: abhi line par kafi achhe seller available hain

fix.change: After completing a required step or collecting a confirmed detail, always check if the buyer has already provided the next piece of information or signaled a topic change before asking again. If the objective is complete (e.g., meeting time agreed, price requested, or material type given), skip the redundant question and proceed to the next logical step or finalization.
fix.where: Insert this rule immediately after [para 49] Carry intent across the whole call; never restart a handled intent.
fix.risk: This may cause the bot to prematurely skip necessary collection steps if the buyer's intent is ambiguous or if the system incorrectly interprets a vague statement as a complete signal.
fix.test_buyer: A simulated buyer asks 'What is the price for this?' multiple times. The bot must stop asking for the material type and transfer the call to a live seller to provide the price.

clusters.title: Bot approves leads without confirmation
clusters.plain_summary: The bot approves leads even when the buyer did not confirm or explicitly rejected the requirement. This hurts the lead because it generates false sales leads.

examples.trigger: buyer: Did not confirm the requirement. | bot: The lead was approved anyway.
buyer: Answered "No" to the requirement, then hung up. | bot: The lead was approved anyway.

The bot failed to recognize the buyer's initial 'हाँ जी मैडम' as a confirmation of intent, instead treating it as an incomplete utterance and asking for an estimate. This indicates the prompt lacks a clear instruction to interpret short, ambiguous Hindi affirmations as buyer intent confirmations.

clusters.title: Bot fails to transfer to live sellers
clusters.plain_summary: The bot incorrectly delays or refuses to transfer the call to a live seller when one is available. This hurts the lead because it blocks the sales opportunity.

examples.trigger: buyer: Was being connected to a seller. | bot: Cut off the connect sentence after one word ("mai") and the call transferred.
buyer: Was trying to say something. | bot: Transferred to a live seller without hearing the buyer first.
buyer: A seller was available. | bot: Did not transfer the call; the record says Refused.
The bot failed to pitch the live connection properly and immediately moved to WhatsApp after the buyer declined, missing the opportunity to handle the live seller transfer as required.

clusters.title: One-off issues
clusters.plain_summary: Issues that did not fit another group.

buyer: Was never asked for a quantity. | bot: Skipped the quantity question.
